ActiveLevel.description: The logic level that turns something on.

Board.description:
A board definition, the same in the catalog and in custom boards files:
the board's name, its FPGA and the ways to program it. The FPGA is one of
the catalog's, which has every FPGA the toolchain supports, so a custom
board adds a board and its programming, never an FPGA.

fpga_id.description:
The board's FPGA, as a catalog ID such as ice40hx4k-tq144-8k
(get_catalog lists them).

pin_groups.description:
What the board wires to FPGA pins, in groups, as in the catalog,
such as its clock and LEDs. Optional.

variants.description:
The ways the board can be programmed, as in the catalog. The first is
the default.

Board.title: Board

LedKind.description: A group of LEDs whose pins mean more than bit numbers.

oneOf.description: One RGB LED: three pins, red, green, blue.

PinGroup.description:
Pins the board wires to one thing, such as its clock or a row of LEDs.
The group's name is the design's port name: a vector, name[N-1:0], for
several pins (the first pin is bit 0), and a plain port for one.

active.description:
The logic level that turns the LEDs on: high or low. Omitted when
not known.

io_standard.description:
The pins' I/O standard, such as LVCMOS33, for pin file formats that
name one (ECP5, Gowin and Xilinx). Omitted when not known or not
needed.

kind.description:
For LEDs whose pins mean more than bit numbers: rgb is one RGB LED,
three pins in the order red, green, blue. Omitted for plain LEDs.

mhz.description: The clock's frequency in MHz, such as 12. Clocks only.

name.description:
The port name, a Verilog identifier unique on the board, such as
sys_clk, led or leds.

pins.description:
The FPGA pins, as the board's pin files name them, such as 49 or
N14. For several pins, the first is bit 0.

type.description:
What the pins are wired to: clock (an oscillator, one pin, with mhz)
or led (LEDs, with active when known). Later versions add types,
such as button and switch.

PinGroupType.description: What a pin group is wired to.

oneOf.description: An oscillator: one pin, with its frequency.

Selector.description:
Which of a board's variants: a value of each standard dimension. In a
board definition it says where the variant sits; in requests
(board_variant) it picks the variant with these values.

connection.description:
How the computer reaches the board: usb, bootloader, ft2232h,
ft232h, cmsis-dap, usb-blaster or unspecified (see the dimensions).

memory.description:
Where the design goes: flash (kept at power-off) or ram (lost at
power-off).

UsbFilter.description: Which USB devices are this board.

pid.description: USB product ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 6010.

product_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's product name must match, when
several boards share the same USB IDs. Omitted means any product name.

release.description:
The device's release number (USB bcdDevice), four lowercase hex
digits, such as 0500, that the device must report, for boards that
share USB IDs but differ in it. On FTDI chips, and on board debuggers
that act like them, it tells the chip type: 0700 for an FT2232H, 0500
for an FT2232C/D or a debugger that acts like one. Omitted means any
release.

serial_regex.description:
A regular expression the device's serial number must match, for
boards that share USB IDs and product names but have serial numbers
that tell them apart. Omitted means any serial number.

vid.description: USB vendor ID, four lowercase hex digits, such as 0403.

Variant.description:
One way to program a board: its selector (its connection and memory),
and how to program the board that way.

args.description:
The programmer's arguments, as a template. The engine replaces
${VID}, ${PID}, ${BUS} and ${DEV} with the device's USB vendor ID,
product ID, bus and device number, ${SERIAL_NUM} with its serial number,
${USB_PATH} with its USB port path (such as 1-2.3, as dfu-util's -p
takes it), and ${BITSTREAM} with the bitstream path.

maintainer_notes.description:
For the board definition's maintainers: where the settings come from
and why they changed. Optional. get_catalog never returns it.

programmer.description: The programmer to run: openfpgaloader, iceprog, dfu-util or icesprog.

selector.description:
The variant's value of each standard dimension, such as
{"connection": "usb", "memory": "flash"}: what board_variant gives
in requests to pick it. No two variants of a board have the same.

tested.description:
Whether programming this way is known to work: tested on the board,
or used unchanged in a tool that relies on it. False for ways that
haven't been tried on hardware, such as a board moved to a different
programmer.

usb.description: The USB filter that finds the board's device.

user_notes.description:
Warnings and missing information for users, such as a USB filter that
also matches other boards or a step needed before programming.

description: FPGA board definitions for the Logix Engine: a map of board IDs (lowercase letters, digits and hyphens) to board definitions. The format of the Logix Engine's board catalog and of custom boards files.

$schema.description: This schema's address, so editors can check the file. Optional; when given, the Logix Engine requires this value.
